package_info.package_versions: all published versions (2021-2022, see dataset for specifics)
package_info.why_malicious: All published versions of this package are malicious because they were mass-published solely to distribute phishing links via package metadata (such as descriptions and readmes). These links lure users to credential-harvesting and scam sites, and are designed to boost the SEO of phishing infrastructure. The packages contain no legitimate code or functionality.

execution_context.trigger: When package metadata is parsed (during install-time, search-time, or when viewing package details in the registry or client UI)
execution_context.file_location: Package description field (e.g., .nuspec for NuGet, package.json for NPM, setup.py metadata for PyPI)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Click Here To Get More Info 🔴➡️ https://gamecodeclaim.com/c/psngenerator/

Click The Link To Get All Access 🔴➡️ https://gamecodeclaim.com/c/psngenerator/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When package metadata is displayed to the user (trigger), the description field renders enticing phishing links (technical_action), which are visible to anyone browsing or searching the package (data_flow), leading users to click and be redirected to external phishing sites where credentials or personal information may be harvested (outcome).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package embeds external, unrelated URLs in its metadata, specifically in the description field, which is a well-known phishing and SEO abuse tactic. The links promise free codes or cheats, enticing users to visit phishing sites.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate package descriptions provide documentation, usage instructions, or links to official project resources. They do not contain unrelated, enticing links to external domains, especially those associated with scams or phishing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may include links to documentation, project homepages, or official support forums, but never to unrelated 'free code', 'hack', or 'generator' sites.
key_indicators: Presence of external URLs in package metadata fields (description, readme) that are unrelated to the package's stated purpose
Use of enticement language such as 'free', 'hack', 'generator', 'cheat', or 'get all access'
Links to known phishing or scam domains (e.g., gamecodeclaim.com)
Absence of any functional or legitimate code in the package
Mass publication of similarly named packages with only metadata changes

attack_chain.action: Automated creation and publication of thousands of packages with enticing names and phishing links embedded in their descriptions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages appear in registry search results and are indexed by search engines, increasing visibility.

attack_chain.action: User or automated system views package details, causing the phishing link in the description to be displayed.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is exposed to the phishing link and may be enticed to click.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the phishing link and is redirected to an external phishing site, which may simulate a 'cheat' or 'generator' and prompt for credentials or personal information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft, scam, or referral reward for the attacker.

attack_chain.action: Some phishing sites further redirect to eCommerce platforms with referral IDs, generating financial rewards for the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives referral bonuses or store credit.

behavioral_signatures: Package descriptions or readmes containing external URLs unrelated to the package's stated functionality
Descriptions promising cheats, hacks, free codes, followers, or similar enticements
Mass publication of similarly named packages with only metadata changes and no functional code
file_indicators: Package metadata fields (description, readme) containing suspicious or unrelated URLs
Package names referencing 'hack', 'generator', 'free', 'cheat', 'codes', or similar terms
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package metadata fields (description, readme) for external URLs, especially those matching known phishing or scam domains or containing enticement language. Flag packages that lack functional code and only provide external links. Monitor for mass-published packages with similar naming patterns and descriptions. Cross-reference discovered URLs against threat intelligence feeds and block or flag packages referencing known malicious domains.
